question: What do we use for report search today, and why did we move off Elasticsearch?
gold_answer: Postgres full-text search (ADR-0012, March 2026, plus pg_trgm from ADR-0015). ES was dropped because there were 2.1M reports not the projected 10M, keeping it in sync caused incidents (2025-12-04 outage), permission filtering was duplicated, and it cost $1,380/month; Postgres FTS had p95 38 ms, within the 150 ms budget.

question: Where is Larkspur hosted?
gold_answer: AWS: ECS Fargate with RDS Postgres, ElastiCache and S3 (ADR-0010, Nov 2025). Heroku (ADR-0003) was superseded and decommissioned on 2025-12-03.

question: Which authentication provider do we use?
gold_answer: WorkOS (AuthKit, SSO, Directory Sync/SCIM) per ADR-0013 (May 2026). Auth0 (ADR-0004) was superseded and its SDK removed in June 2026.

question: How does the web app manage server state?
gold_answer: TanStack Query (persisted to IndexedDB) for server state and Zustand for client state (ADR-0011, Feb 2026). Redux Toolkit (ADR-0006) was superseded and removed in March 2026.

question: What do we use to render inspection reports to PDF?
gold_answer: Playwright with headless Chromium in the worker-pdf queue, since January 2026. It replaced wkhtmltopdf.

question: Is Elasticsearch still used anywhere?
gold_answer: No. The ES client and indexer were removed on 2026-04-14 and the Elastic Cloud deployment was deleted; the tech radar lists it as Retired.

question: How do we handle fuzzy or misspelled address search?
gold_answer: With pg_trgm trigram similarity on a normalized address combined with FTS rank (ADR-0015, Sept 2026). Not Elasticsearch fuzziness any more.

question: Are we building a native iOS or Android app?
gold_answer: No. We stay with the offline-first PWA (ADR-0008); re-confirmed on 2026-04-28 by Inês after a customer request. Revisit at 50 enterprise seats on one customer or an MDM requirement.

question: Which ADR is the current decision for report search: ADR-0005 or ADR-0012?
gold_answer: ADR-0012 (Postgres FTS), amended by ADR-0015. ADR-0005 (Elasticsearch) is superseded.

question: Do we use GraphQL for the public API?
gold_answer: No. REST with /v1 path versioning (ADR-0007). A GraphQL proposal was rejected in September 2025 because the offline service worker cache can't sensibly cache POSTs to /graphql; nested data uses ?include= instead.

question: How does the PDF worker avoid Chromium cold starts?
gold_answer: It keeps a warm pool of 3 Chromium browsers per task, recycled every 200 renders (added Feb 2026 after slow-PDF tickets).

question: Who decided to use Elasticsearch for search originally?
gold_answer: Jonah Blake proposed it (ADR-0005) and Maya Chen approved it on 2025-04-22; Tomás Rivera had raised concerns.

question: Who approved replacing Elasticsearch with Postgres full-text search?
gold_answer: Priya Natarajan proposed ADR-0012; Maya Chen and Tomás Rivera approved it (merged 2026-03-17).

question: Who decided our pricing model, and what is it?
gold_answer: Inês Duarte, on 2025-07-08: per seat with 40 reports/month included per seat and per-report overage; annual plans get two months free.

question: Who made the call not to build a native iOS app for Harbor & Pine Inspections?
gold_answer: Inês Duarte closed it as not planned on 2026-04-28, with input from Lena, Sam and Maya.

question: Who decided to move off Heroku, and who led the migration?
gold_answer: Kofi Mensah proposed ADR-0010 and led the migration; Maya Chen and Tomás Rivera approved; Inês Duarte signed off on cost.

question: Who decided against GraphQL?
gold_answer: Maya Chen closed Sam Whitfield's GraphQL proposal on 2025-09-12, after Tomás Rivera argued for REST with ?include=.

question: Who approved switching to WorkOS, and who signed off on the cost?
gold_answer: Ravi Kapoor proposed ADR-0013, Maya Chen approved it, and Inês Duarte signed off on the per-connection pricing.

question: Who decided how conflicting offline edits are resolved, and how?
gold_answer: Maya Chen: per-field last-writer-wins plus a conflict banner; CRDTs (Yjs) were deferred. Lena Park implemented it.

question: Who needs to approve an ADR?
gold_answer: The CTO (Maya Chen) plus an engineer who will own the change; vendor decisions over $500/month also need a thumbs-up from the CEO (Inês Duarte).

question: Who took over search after Jonah left?
gold_answer: Priya Natarajan (Tomás Rivera took PDFs), per Jonah's handoff notes in Oct 2025.

question: Why did we pick Heroku in the first place?
gold_answer: No platform engineer, git-push deploys and managed Postgres/Redis with backups, to ship the pilot in April 2025. Exit criteria: bill over ~$2k/month or private networking.

question: Why did we move from Heroku to AWS?
gold_answer: The bill hit ~$2,900/month vs ~$1,700 estimated on AWS, PDF workers hit R14/R15 memory errors on 1 GB dynos, an enterprise customer needed VPC peering (Private Spaces), and we had a platform engineer.

question: Why did we originally choose wkhtmltopdf instead of headless Chrome?
gold_answer: A single static binary that was fast (~1.5 s for 30 pages) and worked on Heroku; Chromium needed ~400 MB of dependencies and more memory than the 1 GB dynos had.

question: Why did we replace wkhtmltopdf?
gold_answer: It is archived/unmaintained, can't render CSS grid/flexbox (the photo grid broke), bundles an old Qt WebKit with CVEs, and Fargate's 4 GB PDF worker removed the memory constraint.

question: Why Celery rather than RQ or Dramatiq for background jobs?
gold_answer: Celery has retries with backoff, beat scheduling and queue routing (PDFs on their own queue); RQ lacks scheduling and nobody had run Dramatiq in production.

question: Why do new tables use UUIDv7 primary keys?
gold_answer: Offline clients must create ids before the server sees them; sequential ints need a round trip and leak volume; UUIDv4 fragments B-tree indexes (2.3x slower inserts) while UUIDv7 is within 8% of bigint.

question: Why version the API in the URL path instead of a header?
gold_answer: The PWA's service worker cache keys on the URL, so header versions would collide in the offline cache.

question: Why did we leave Auth0?
gold_answer: Enterprise customers needed SAML SSO and SCIM; on Auth0 that required the Enterprise plan (~4x the bill) plus a SCIM add-on. WorkOS's per-connection pricing fits our per-firm enterprise plans.

question: Why did we build a PWA instead of native mobile apps?
gold_answer: Inspectors need full offline capture in basements; two frontend engineers can't maintain web plus two native apps with app store releases; customers asked for offline reliability, not app store presence.

question: Why is API rate limiting done in the app instead of AWS WAF?
gold_answer: WAF limits per IP and partners call from shared cloud IPs; we need per-API-key and per-plan limits only the app knows. WAF stays as a coarse DDoS backstop.

question: Why did we drop Redux?
gold_answer: About 80% of the store was cached server data with hand-written loading flags, invalidation and optimistic updates; lots of boilerplate per screen and fragile offline thunk replay.

question: Why do photo originals move to Glacier after 90 days?
gold_answer: Photos are 85% of storage cost and rarely opened after 90 days; reports must be kept 7 years as legal records, so originals go to Glacier Instant Retrieval (ADR-0014).

question: When was Heroku decommissioned?
When did production search switch to Postgres, and when was Elasticsearch removed?
gold_answer: Cutover merged 2026-03-24 (search_backend flag defaulting to postgres); ES code removed and cluster deleted on 2026-04-14.

question: When was the search reindex outage and how bad was it?
gold_answer: 2025-12-04, 02:10 to 11:20 UTC: about 18% of reports (~340k) were missing from search; no data loss.

question: When were users migrated from Auth0 to WorkOS?
gold_answer: Tuesday 2026-06-09 at 07:00 UTC, importing password hashes so nobody had to reset.

question: When did Stripe billing ship, and what pricing does it implement?
gold_answer: Merged 2025-07-15: per-seat subscriptions with 40 reports/month per seat and metered per-report overage.

question: What's the evidence that Postgres full-text search is fast enough for us?
gold_answer: The Feb 2026 spike on 2.1M reports: p95 38 ms vs 22 ms on ES (budget 150 ms) with 91% top-10 overlap; the shadow-read on 61k real queries: p95 41 ms, 93% overlap.

question: What was the root cause of the December 2025 search outage?
gold_answer: The reindex swapped the alias as soon as the bulk load was enqueued, not finished, and the 2-node Elastic Cloud cluster then hit its disk watermark and stalled.

question: How much money did removing Elasticsearch save?
gold_answer: About $1,380 per month (the 3-node Elastic Cloud deployment).

question: Did anyone object to Elasticsearch when it was chosen?
gold_answer: Yes. Tomás Rivera requested changes on ADR-0005: a second datastore to sync, a reindex procedure and duplicated permission rules; he suggested Postgres FTS.

question: What evidence is there that permission filtering in Elasticsearch drifted from Postgres?
gold_answer: Sept 2025: inspectors who changed teams still saw the old team's reports in search; the March 2026 shadow-read found 14 ES hits that Postgres correctly hid.

question: What did the engineer who proposed Elasticsearch say about it when he left, and what happened to it afterwards?
gold_answer: Jonah Blake's handoff (Oct 2025) said that at ~1.4M reports Postgres FTS might have been enough. In March 2026 Priya replaced ES with Postgres FTS (ADR-0012).

question: Which constraint led us to wkhtmltopdf, and which infrastructure change removed it?
gold_answer: Chromium didn't fit in 1 GB Heroku dynos; the move to ECS Fargate (ADR-0010) gave the PDF worker 4 GB, which made the Playwright switch possible.

question: Which postmortem action item led to an ADR, and what did that ADR decide?
gold_answer: Action item 3 of the 2025-12-04 search postmortem ('evaluate whether we need Elasticsearch') led to the evaluation issue and ADR-0012: replace ES with Postgres FTS.

question: ADR-0004 came with a warning about a limitation. Did it come true, and what did we do?
gold_answer: Yes: SAML was only on Auth0's top plans. In 2026 enterprise deals required SAML and SCIM, so we moved to WorkOS (ADR-0013).

question: What follow-up did the move to Postgres search require, and who raised it?
gold_answer: Misspelled addresses stopped matching; Inês raised it from support tickets in July 2026 and Priya added pg_trgm fuzzy matching (ADR-0015).

question: How is the UUIDv7 decision connected to the offline photo outbox?
gold_answer: Outbox entries carry client-generated ids so the API can dedupe retried uploads; ADR-0009 chose UUIDv7 so clients can create those ids offline without collisions.

question: Did Tomás's 2025 concern about Elasticsearch turn out to matter?
gold_answer: Yes. Sync problems caused three search incidents (mapping limit, team-move permissions, the Dec 2025 outage) and ES was replaced; Tomás approved ADR-0012 noting he had argued for Postgres FTS in April 2025.

question: Have we decided to move background jobs off Celery to a Postgres-backed queue?
gold_answer: No. It's an open discussion (Sept 2026); Redis stays anyway for rate limiting and the team prefers to wait for a concrete problem.

question: Do we use a feature flag vendor?
gold_answer: No. We use a home-grown feature_flags table; LaunchDarkly was quoted at ~$700/month and the question is still open.
